I'm sorry to hear that. Feeling resentment for both your husband's loss of work and your son's loss of his job is entirely understandable.
I have a hard time not dwelling on the negative things going on.  It's hard to see anything positive or feel hopeful for the future.
I have an adult son who also lost his job recently, and I understand the added stress that can cause in your household.
That is a really difficult position to be in.

My son is very defiant and argues with us about everything we try and get him to do, but he expects us to give him money for fun things that he wants to do when he isn't willing to work or even help out around the house

It is hard to keep my emotions separate from what is going on with him
That is very understandable! Setting boundaries for yourself may help. Even when it's difficult, being clear with your son that you will not be giving him money could help.
Sometimes being clear with your own expectations can help him to see what won't be accepted from him as long as he is living in your home.

I feel guilty sometimes taking time to do things that I like and that are away from my family.  I can see that I need to do that more, though.

Thank you, it is helpful to know that other people have felt the same way.

Hi I am seeking support to assist me with better sleep patterns.
Hi there, let me get a deeper understanding of your existing sleep pattern. Do you suffer from insomnia or another type of sleep disorder?
No, it is not insomnia.
Okay, are you drinking enough water and eating a healthy diet?
I could improve my water intake and eat more vegatables.
I like to analyze my own habits every now and then, it helps me stay in check. You can definitely benefit from meditating and self reflecting.
Thanks!  What other ideas do you have?

Of course! I always knock right out after a workout. But if you aren't able to, just simple things like turning all the lights off at the same time every night and laying in bed will help. It will align your circadian rhythm!
Great, but I wake up frequently thinking about the recent events surrounding police and how they treat black people.

It definitely is a valid reason to be kept awake. The only good part about something so horrible, is that you have the power to make sure you will continue to be a good person. If everyone was as empathetic as you, the world would be a better place. Thank you for caring so deeply about such a brutal matter.
I wish there were more caring people in the world.

Kindness is contagious, and you definitely have a kind heart. As long as you remain soft in a hard world, people will recognize that and follow suit. The world is becoming more aware, and we have the power to raise future generations with more knowledge and love for one another. Caring doesn't come naturally to many unfortunately, but the ways of inspiring the people that don't care, are endless. We as a society can definitely think of more ways to care for one another.
Correct, but having a kind heart does not keep me from waking up & worrying about my son and other black men in my family.
I worry about my sons and husband and father all the time... I shift my focus on loving them and cherishing every moment we have together. Police or not, the time we have is not promised..
That's good advice.
Are you still there?

A hot cup of tea never hurt too! But in all seriousness, I can completely understand your sleep troubles. It is much deeper than just that. Perspective is the key to life. You are a strong and empathetic soul.
okay
Love conquers all
That is so beautifully true
I'm looking forward to a fulls night rest.
That is good, lavender baths or showers will also ease and relax the troubled mind.
Relaxing is good therapy.
I like to relax with a book and a blanket sometimes too.
Self care is needed.
Self care is definitely something we can overlook accidentally. Being self aware is a daily practice.
I agree.  Loving ourselves & the ones we care about too.
It is good that we spoke today, I am going to hug my sons a little harder when I see them tonight.
Hey, are you around? I could really use someone to talk to.
Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's going on?
Bob and I had a big argument last night. I haven't been able to stop thinking about it.
I'm sorry to hear that. Arguments can be really tough. Do you want to share what happened?
Yeah, it just spiraled out of control. We started talking about our finances, and it just got heated.
Financial pressures can put so much strain on relationships. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed. How are you feeling now?
Exhausted, honestly. It's like we're stuck in this cycle of stress, and I don't see a way out.
It sounds really challenging, Emily. It's okay to feel this way. Have you two been able to talk it out since it happened?
Not yet. We both needed some space. Bob went for a drive, and I've just been trying to calm down.
Taking some space can be helpful to gather thoughts. Do you think you’ll be ready to talk soon?
I hope so. I don't want to keep ignoring it, but I'm also scared it'll turn into another argument.
That's understandable. Talking during a calm moment might help. Maybe planning a time to chat could prevent it from escalating?
That's a good idea. Maybe after dinner tonight. I just wish he would understand how stressed I am too.
Your feelings are very valid, Emily. It's important for both of you to feel heard. Do you feel like you can express how you’re both feeling?
I want to, but sometimes I don’t know how to start without sounding like I’m blaming him.
Starting with 'I feel' statements can help focus on your emotions rather than assigning blame. It's okay to express vulnerability.
That's true. I'll try that. Thanks for reminding me. I just want us to be okay.
You’re doing your best, and that is important. Figuring it out together might bring you closer. How are you taking care of yourself today?
I haven’t really done much for myself yet. Maybe I should go for a walk or listen to some music.
That sounds like a wonderful idea. Taking a little time for self-care can help clear your mind and give you strength.
Thanks for listening. It really helps just having someone to talk to about all this.
I'm always here for you, Emily. Take it one step at a time, and keep me updated if you need anything.
I will. Thanks again.
Hey, I needed someone to talk to about everything that's been going on.
Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. How have things been since you started therapy?
It's been a bit overwhelming, to be honest. I'm glad I took the step, but it's a lot to unpack.
It sounds like you're processing a lot. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed. What's been on your mind?
Mainly my relationship with Bob and the financial strain. It's hard not to feel angry and resentful sometimes.
That's understandable. Financial pressures can really strain relationships. How are you both handling it right now?
We're trying to talk more without arguing, but it's a struggle. I can't help but feel frustrated thinking about how he left his job.
I can hear the frustration and it's valid. It must be tough carrying the burden alone. How is the therapy helping you with these feelings?
Therapy helps, slowly. It's nice to have a space to express myself, but it doesn't change things immediately at home.
Having an outlet is important. Therapy can sometimes take time, but it's great you're making progress. Are there things you're learning that help?
I learned about setting boundaries and communicating my needs. It’s something I’m working on with Bob.
That sounds like a positive step. How is Bob responding to the changes you're trying to make?
I think he's trying, but it's hard to change old habits, especially when both of us are stressed.
Change is challenging, especially during tough times. Acknowledging the effort on both sides is a good step. What about your job? How's that affecting things?
Work is another stress. They doubled my workload after an acquisition, but no raise came with it.
That sounds incredibly unfair and stressful. No wonder you feel overwhelmed with everything piling up.
It is. I'm trying to manage my mental health, but sometimes it feels like too much.
It's okay to feel that way. It seems like you're doing your best despite everything. Are you able to find any small ways to de-stress?
I try to take walks and focus on mindfulness exercises. They help me feel a little more grounded.
That's great to hear. It's important to celebrate these small wins. I'll be here to support you as you navigate through this.
Hey Emily, it's been a little while. How are you doing?
Hi, it's been... a tough week.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
Yeah, actually. My son Jerry got in trouble at school. They caught him using his phone inappropriately.
That sounds really stressful. How did you find out about it?
We had a meeting with the school's principal. It was embarrassing, especially after telling him so many times to focus on his studies.
I can imagine how difficult that must have been for you. How did the meeting go?
It was tense. The principal was understanding but firm. I just felt so disappointed and a bit like I've failed him.
It's understandable to feel that way, but you haven't failed him. You're a caring mother who's trying her best.
Thank you. I've been trying to figure out how to handle this. The financial strain with Bob, and now Jerry acting out... it's just a lot.
That does sound overwhelming. How have you been managing everything?
Therapy helps, but outside of that, I just try to keep my head above water.
I'm glad you've found some support in therapy. What strategies have been helping you there?
The therapist has been teaching me breathing techniques and we've been working on expressing my feelings more constructively.
That sounds really valuable. Do you think any of those techniques could help with how you're feeling about Jerry?
Perhaps. I think I need to communicate better with him and find out what's really going on beneath the surface.
It sounds like you have a great approach. Being able to talk openly with him might really help both of you.
I hope so. I just want to make sure he understands that I care about him, even when I’m upset.
He’s fortunate to have you watching out for him. If you ever need to talk more about any of this, I’m here for you.
Thank you. It means a lot to have someone to lean on right now.
Hey, I really needed someone to talk to today.
Of course, Emily. I'm here to listen. What's on your mind?
I just got this awful performance review today. My boss said my stress is impacting my work.
I'm so sorry to hear that. It sounds really tough, especially since you've been dealing with so much lately.
Yeah, it's been overwhelming. Ever since the company acquisition, I've been drowning in work and I didn't even get a raise.
That sounds incredibly frustrating. Having more to do without additional compensation feels unfair.
Exactly. And then there's the constant tension at home. Bob and I argued about finances again last month.
That must be adding so much stress to your life. It's hard when multiple areas feel out of balance.
It really is. I feel like I'm failing my son too. His trouble at school didn't help.
You're carrying a lot on your shoulders. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed with all these responsibilities.
Thank you for saying that. I went back to therapy last month, and it's been helping a bit.
That's a great step, Emily. Taking time for yourself and seeking help is important.
It is. But I feel like I'm just plastering over cracks. Every day feels like a battle.
It sounds exhausting. Is there any aspect of your day that brings you a bit of peace?
Sometimes, just the quiet moments before everyone wakes up. It's short but calm.
Hold onto those moments. They can serve as a reminder that peace is possible amid the chaos.
I will. Just talking to you has made me feel a little lighter.
I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, you're not alone in this. I'm always here to listen.
Thank you so much. It means a lot to have someone who understands.
Hey Emily, how are you doing today?
Hi, honestly I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed today.
I'm sorry to hear that. Is it what's happening at work that's on your mind?
Yeah, the company announced a potential restructuring, and it's got me really anxious about what's to come.
That sounds incredibly stressful. Have they given any details about how it might affect your position?
Not really, just that things might change soon. It just feels like one more thing I can't control.
That uncertainty can be so hard. It's understandable to feel out of control right now. How are you managing otherwise?
I'm trying to just keep everything together. It’s hard when I’ve got stuff going on with Bob and with Jerry too.
Between work, home life, and everything else, it makes sense why you're feeling this way. Is Bob supportive during all of this?
We’re both stressed with money issues, and we've been arguing more. It's tough on both of us.
That sounds really challenging. Have you been able to talk about these concerns in therapy?
Yes, my therapist is great, but sometimes I feel like there's so much to unpack that it's overwhelming.
It's good to have that support though. It’s okay to take things one step at a time, even if it feels slow.
I know you’re right. I just worry about how all of this stress is affecting my job performance. The last review from my boss wasn't great.
The performance review must have been hard to take. But remember, that's just one part of you. What you've persevered through is something you should be proud of.
Thanks. It’s just hard when it feels like I'm not doing enough at work, and then things at home aren’t great either.
You're doing your best, and that counts for a lot. Have you had any moments recently where you found some peace or relief?
I guess there's been small moments, like when I take a walk or read a book before bed.
That's wonderful. Those small moments are so valuable. It's important to keep finding those times for yourself.
I should focus more on that, even if it's hard sometimes. Thank you for listening.
Always here to listen, Emily. Don’t hesitate to reach out when you need to talk, okay?
I will. Thank you so much for being there.
Hey, can we talk? I could really use someone to listen right now.
Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's going on?
Well, Bob finally got a part-time job, which should be a good thing, right?
It's a step forward, but it sounds like you're feeling a lot more than just relief. What's on your mind?
I thought I'd feel better, but instead, I just feel overwhelmed. Like things are barely holding together.
That makes sense, considering everything you've been dealing with lately. It's a lot to carry.
Exactly. It's just this constant stress. Bob's part-time gig helps a bit with money, but I can't help feeling frustrated that it took so long.
It's understandable to feel that way. It's been a tough road for you, especially with the financial stress.
Yeah, and it doesn't help that my job feels so unstable. I worry all the time about whether I'll be able to keep it.
The job uncertainty adds another layer of stress. It's okay to have those concerns.
Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for the next thing to go wrong. It's exhausting.
Feeling trapped in that cycle is really tough. Have you been able to talk about this with your therapist?
I have. We've been working on it. I think I just struggle with knowing where to even start making changes.
Taking those first steps can be daunting. It's great that you're seeking help and trying to navigate through this.
Thanks. It's just hard when the people around me feel like they're adding to the weight instead of helping.
That sounds isolating. It’s important to have support from those around you. Have there been any positive moments between you and Bob lately?
Well, we did have a decent conversation about budgeting yesterday. It felt productive.
That's great to hear. Even small constructive talks can help rebuild some connection.
You're right. I guess I need to focus on those moments more and not get swallowed by the bigger picture.
Exactly. Celebrating small victories can help lighten the load a bit. You’re doing the best you can.
Thanks for saying that. It helps to hear it out loud. I forget sometimes.
I’m happy to remind you anytime. You're strong and capable, Emily.
Thank you. I appreciate you being here for me.
Always here to lend an ear whenever you need it. Take care, Emily.
I will. Talk to you soon.
Hey, I really need to talk. Things have been so overwhelming lately.
I'm here for you, Emily. What's been going on?
Jerry left us. It was so sudden after a huge argument, and I feel lost.
I'm so sorry to hear that. It must be incredibly hard for you. Do you want to talk about what led to the disagreement?
We were arguing about his lack of responsibility and how he's ignoring his future. Maybe I was too harsh.
It sounds like you're worried about his well-being and future, which is completely understandable. How are you feeling about the situation now?
I'm torn. Part of me feels guilty, but another part feels exhausted from all the stress we've been through.
It's okay to feel mixed emotions. You're dealing with a lot on your plate—work, family, and financial pressures. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed.
Yeah, with Bob's job, Jerry's incident at school, and all... it feels never-ending. I just want a break.
You've been through an extraordinary amount. Can your therapy sessions provide a space to process these feelings?
They're helpful, but it's hard to shake the constant anxiety. I just wish Jerry was back home so we could work things out.
It sounds like you really value the connection with your family. Have you tried reaching out to Jerry since he left?
I have, but he hasn't responded. It breaks my heart knowing he's out there, upset and alone.
Feeling powerless in this situation can be stressful. Is there anyone else you can lean on for support during this time?
Bob's trying his best, but we both feel so drained. It's tough to even find time for us to talk deeply anymore.
Finding moments to connect amidst the chaos sounds challenging. Maybe even small shared moments with Bob could provide some comfort?
That's true. Even just sitting together, watching something light, might ease the tension.
That sounds like a good start. Remember, you're doing your best in a tough situation. It's okay to take small steps and be kind to yourself.
Thank you, that really helps. I guess I just have to keep trying and hope things will get better.
Absolutely, Emily. Keep holding on to that hope, and I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.
Hey there, I guess I just needed to talk today.
Of course, Emily. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
Well, I got an unexpected compliment from my boss today about my recent performance at work.
That sounds like a positive development! How does that make you feel?
Relieved, to some extent. It's been a while since I've felt good about my work.
It's understandable given the increased workload and stress you've faced. It's great to hear some recognition is coming your way. What do you think brought about the compliment?
I think I've finally adapted a bit to the changes after the acquisition, and I've been trying really hard to stay focused, even though it's tough with everything else going on.
You've been putting in a lot of effort, and it shows. It's not easy to balance work stress with personal struggles. How have things been at home?
Things with Bob are still stressful, with the financial strains and all. His part-time job has helped some, but there's still tension.
Relationships can be challenging, especially under financial pressure. Have you two had any discussions about how to move forward?
We talk... but it's mostly arguments. I feel like we're both just at our wits' end sometimes.
It sounds really tough. Disagreements are hard, but it can be helpful to approach it as a team, looking for solutions together. Do you think that's possible?
I hope so. It's just hard to communicate when we're both stressed and upset.
Stress can definitely make communication harder. Your therapist might have some strategies that could help when you're feeling overwhelmed.
Yeah, I'll mention it next time I see her. It could be helpful to have some new approaches.
That's a great idea. How is everything going with your son and his situation at school?
's still having a tough time. He's grounded after the incident at school, and that's affecting us too. I just wish things could be simpler.
That sounds really tough on all of you. It's okay to feel overwhelmed by everything. You mentioned Jerry left home after a disagreement too—how are you handling that?
Honestly, I feel a mix of anger, sadness, and worry. I know he's an adult, but I wish he hadn't left like that.
It's completely natural to have those feelings, Emily. You're a caring mother, and wanting your child close is understandable. Have you been able to reach out to him since then?
Not much. He needs space, I think. It's just hard to not be able to help him when he needs it.
That must be really tough. Giving him space while being there if he needs support is a good balance. Try to focus on being ready for when he's ready to reconnect.
Thanks for saying that. It's been a lot to handle, but I'm trying to stay hopeful.
Hope is important. Taking things one step at a time can make it more manageable. Is there anything specific that's helped you manage your stress lately?
I've started walking in the mornings to clear my head. It’s not much, but I think it helps.
That sounds like a healthy habit. Small steps forward are definitely progress. Remember, I'm always here when you need to talk. You don't have to face things alone.
Thank you. It's nice to know I have your support.

current_prefix.text: Hey Anna, it's good to see you online. How are you doing today?
Hi... honestly, not so great. It's been a rough week.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
Yeah, I had an argument with my parents about my future plans, and it got really intense.
That sounds tough. What was the argument about, if you're comfortable sharing?
They want me to focus on getting into a good university, but I'm not even sure what I want to study yet.
It can be really overwhelming when you're not sure about your path, and there's pressure from others. How did that make you feel?
I just felt trapped and like I was disappointing them. It reminded me of the fight I had with my boyfriend about future plans too.
It's natural to feel that way when expectations feel piled up. How's everything with your boyfriend now?
We haven't really resolved things. It's this limbo where everything feels uncertain, and now my parents add to that stress.
That sounds like so much to carry all at once, Anna. It’s understandable to feel overwhelmed. What do you feel you need right now?
I think I need to figure out what I actually want for my future without feeling like I'm letting everyone down.
That's a really important realization. It's your future, after all. Have you had any thoughts about what interests or excites you?
I love art and writing, but I'm not sure if that's practical. It feels risky compared to more traditional paths.

Everyone deals with pressure differently, and it's okay to feel like you're struggling. You're handling a lot.
Thank you for saying that. I just keep overthinking everything, like doubting my abilities in writing and studies.
Your feelings are valid. You're really talented, but sometimes anxiety can make you doubt what you're capable of.
It's just hard to remember that when I feel so stuck. And isolation during exam week hasn't helped.
Being isolated can definitely amplify those feelings. Do you have anyone you could reach out to for support?
I guess I could talk to some classmates. We've been good study buddies in the past.
That sounds like a great idea. Having a support system can make a huge difference.
I'll try reaching out. I just hope I can keep it together for the rest of the exams.
Taking one day at a time might help. I'm here whenever you need to talk though, okay?
I appreciate that, a lot. I didn't realize how much I needed to vent until now.
I'm glad you reached out. You're doing your best, and that's something to be proud of.
Thanks for listening. It means more than you know.
Anytime, Taylor. Let's catch up soon and see how you're feeling after exams, okay?
Sounds good. I'll talk to you then.

That sounds like a big step. How do you feel about reconnecting with her?
I feel relieved in some ways. We've both grown and matured since our breakup, but it's also scary.
It's understandable to have mixed feelings. What scares you about it?
I guess I'm afraid of falling back into the same patterns we had before.

turns.text: How are you today?
I'm doing pretty good.

Yah they are very difficult.
How have you been managing everything?
Fine I've been pretty much just trying to go out as little as possible and stay safe.

Yes I would have to agree.

Yeah I'm staying with them for the holidays and then going back home in January.
I imagine that can create some stress?
No not really it's all good over here.

Yes because I am on winter break now.
I assume that means you're in college then? So the stress of finals is over now?
Yes I am. And yeah I just finished finals.
That's good, I hope they went well for you.
They did. Some were hard, but at least they're over now.
Yes, now you can relax and spend time with your family without the added stress.
Yes, exactly.
Well I hope you and your family enjoy the holidays and stay safe.
Thank you, you too.
Thanks so much!
Are you with family?
Yes, just my immediate family.
Oh that's good. Staying safe.
Absolutely, the best thing we can do right now. Even though it's kind of a bummer.
Yeah, hopefully things will go back to normal soon.
I hope so too, this has been such a crazy year.
I agree.
Hi, what I can help you with today?
Hi
I had problems in the past and somehow right now
What sort of problems were in your past and now?
I loved physics and I decided to attend university, but soon after I slowly lost my interest and became unmotivated
What was happening in your life that made you lose interest?
Actually the professors and the class atmosphere was the reason, and of course the quality of teaching
so I started to skipping the classes and failing

Yes lots of stress and pressure. I did not, because we didn't have such things or at least I wasn't aware
But nobody even pointed that why I'm failing, they just didn't care
I agree it is a lot of pressure, but do not let bad teachers deter you. I would reach out to a school counselor and let them know your situation. Every school must have one.
Also, physics is a difficult course to study, but if you chose it, that means you have a very strong mind.
I loved physics a lot more than now, but what's the point of studying when the teachers are pulsing you not to study! (because of the quality of teaching)
I hope there was someone, but I don't think we have a counselor
More reason to speak to a school counselor or school administrator. We need to provide help to students, not have bad teachers deter them.
Yeah, same with me! I wish I could attend a better univeristy
What made you choose this particular university you are at?
I didn't have another choice but this
Have you looked into other Universities for the possibility of transferring
Hmmm, actually I didn't think about this option
Just think about what you want in a good university and research from there
Yeah, I should do it
Thanks for the talk
you've been more helpful than my teachers!
You're welcome I hope you find the perfect university for you
Thanks, I wish  you luck in your future endeavours

Goodbye
Hello. Is anyone there

Have you tried confronting them and asking why they are being bullies?
I did and they respond by saying that they are just joking and that I'm handsome. But it's starting to get on my nerves because it's all they make fun about every time they see me!
I'm sure you are very handsome! They could just be jealous.
Haha I would hope so
Still though, it makes me want to avoid them when I go to school on the bus
What do you think I should do then?
I understand, school was tough for me too.
I suggest you tell them to knock it off or you can sit somewhere away from the bus.
Should I just beat them up with my backpack
No, beating them up will only get you in trouble and that won't help.
There's another bus route. Should I just take that instead

You could also tell a teacher what is happening. They will help you out.
I bet you are handsome! Don't let it get to you.

Do you believe working out will help
Working out will help a lot! When I was feeling down on myself I decided to go to the gym three times a week. It was a great confidence boost.
Awesome. I will start to take care of myself and not worry about others then.
That sounds like a fantastic idea.
Hey Nick, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey... I've been feeling pretty down recently.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
Yeah, it's about Henry. We argued again, and this time it got ugly.
That sounds tough. What happened between you two?
It started with some jokes they made. I found them really insensitive and hurtful.
I can understand why that would be upsetting. Did you talk to them about how you felt?
I tried, but it just turned into a shouting match. I didn't expect it would escalate.
That sounds really frustrating. It can be hard when someone you care about doesn't understand your perspective.
Exactly. I mean, we've been friends for so long. I thought we'd be on the same page about these things.
It's natural to feel disappointed in situations like this. It's okay to feel hurt.
Thanks. I just can't help but think if maybe I'm overreacting.
Your feelings are valid, Nick. It's important to acknowledge when something bothers you.
True, but what if I drive him away by holding onto this?
It might help to express why those jokes affected you deeply. If he's a true friend, he should understand and respect your feelings.
Yeah, I think I should try talking to him when things cool down. I don't want to lose our friendship over this.
That sounds like a good plan. Give it some time, and approach it when you're both calmer.
I will. Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk it through.
Anytime, Nick. I'm here whenever you need to chat or get things off your chest.
I appreciate that. Hopefully, next time we'll be talking about something more positive!
I'm sure we will. Hang in there, Nick. You've got this.
Hey Nick, it's nice to see you online. How are you doing today?
Hey, I'm feeling a mix of things actually. There's a lot on my mind.
I’m here to listen. What's been going on?
Well, remember how I had that fallout with Henry because of those jokes?
Yeah, I remember. That was really tough for you both. How’s that been playing out?
We finally talked again, and it was... unexpectedly emotional. We actually sorted things out.
That’s great to hear, Nick! How did the conversation go?
It started off a bit awkward, but we both apologized. We realized how much we missed each other.
Sometimes those tough conversations are what make friendships stronger. You must have felt a lot lighter afterward.
Yeah, I did. But it also made me think about how close I came to losing a really important person in my life.
That realization can be a lot to take in. It sounds like you value that friendship deeply.
I really do. We've been friends for so long, and it just felt wrong not having him around.
It’s understandable. When someone is that integral in your life, their absence can feel enormous.
Exactly. I guess part of me is still worried we might slip back into old patterns.
That's a valid concern. Have you both talked about how to avoid that?
A bit. We agreed to be more open when things bother us, instead of letting them build up.
That sounds like a solid plan. Communication is so key. How are you feeling about that agreement?
Hopeful, mostly. I guess I'm just trying to stay positive about it.
That’s a great mindset, Nick. It takes courage to forgive and move forward.
Thanks. It helps to talk about it, honestly. I guess I needed to process it out loud.
I’m always here for that. It’s important to have spaces to express what you’re going through.
Definitely. It’s nice to know I'm not alone in this.
You’re certainly not alone, Nick. Anytime you need to talk, just reach out.
Thanks again. I really appreciate our chats.
Anytime, Nick. Take care of yourself and keep nurturing that friendship.
Hey, do you have a moment to chat? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed.
Of course, Nick. What's going on?
I've been swamped with assignments, and it's starting to really wear me down.
That sounds really tough. Are these assignments from your physics course?
Yeah, mostly. It's just been so relentless, and I really don't feel any support from the university.
I remember you mentioning before how the teaching quality has been lacking. Has it gotten worse?
Pretty much. It feels like I'm teaching myself. I'm even thinking of dropping the course.
That's such a hard decision. Dropping a course can feel like a big step, but you're the one who knows what's best for you.
Exactly. I just feel like I'm drowning in work with no payoff, you know? It's exhausting.
Definitely. It's important to weigh the pros and cons though. How do you feel about physics overall?
I used to love it, but now it's just become a source of stress. I miss being excited about it.
It's really tough when something you used to love becomes stressful. Is there anything you've considered doing differently to reignite that passion?
I've thought about seeking outside resources or maybe talking to a different professor, but it feels daunting.
That's understandable. Sometimes reaching out for help can feel challenging, but it could make a difference. You shouldn't have to tackle this all alone.
I guess I could try, but I'm worried about failing either way. I hate feeling this uncertain.
It's okay to feel uncertain, Nick. Remember when you and Henry had that fallout and reconciled? You took a brave step then and it worked out.
True, I appreciate you bringing that up. It's nice to remember that things can turn around.
Exactly. You've got the resilience to turn this around too. Maybe start with small steps and see how it feels?
Yeah, maybe reaching out to a professor wouldn't be so bad to start with. Thank you for talking this through with me.
Anytime, Nick. I'm always here to support you in any way I can. Let me know how it goes when you take that first step.
Will do. I'm actually feeling a bit lighter talking about it now.
I'm glad to hear that. Keep taking care of yourself, okay?
Hey Nick, how have you been doing lately?
Hey, it's been a bit tough honestly. I decided to talk to my family about everything that's been happening.
I'm glad you opened up to them. How did that conversation go?
It was a relief in some ways. They listened to me, which was good.
That's great to hear! Did they offer any advice or support?
They did offer support, but it still feels like they don't fully understand the pressure I'm under with my physics course.
I can imagine that's frustrating. Do you feel like you got to express everything you wanted to?
Mostly, yes. But it's hard for them to really grasp the academic stress when they haven't experienced it themselves.
It's definitely tough when others can't fully relate. How are you handling the pressure now?
I'm trying to stay on top of my assignments, but the quality of teaching hasn't improved. It feels like a constant uphill battle.
That sounds really challenging, especially when support isn't available. Have you thought again about possibly dropping the course?
I have, but it's also hard to think about leaving something unfinished. I don't want to feel like I've failed.
It's understandable. Remember, taking a step back doesn't mean you're failing—it can be a strategic move for your well-being.
That's a good point. I just wish there was more support from the university, like better teaching or someone I could talk to.
Have you considered reaching out to a student advisor or counseling services at your university?
I've thought about it, but it's a bit intimidating to take that step. I guess I'm worried about not being taken seriously.
It's totally normal to feel that way. Maybe starting with a small step, like emailing an advisor, could make it feel more manageable.
That sounds like a good way to ease into it. I think I'll give it a try.
I'm proud of you for taking this step, Nick. Remember, I'm here for you and you're not alone in this.
Thanks, I really appreciate it. It helps to know there's someone who understands what I'm going through.
Anytime, Nick. Keep me posted on how things go with the advisor, okay?
Will do. Thanks again for being there for me.
Hey, I guess I just need someone to talk to right now.
Of course, Nick. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
It's about my physics course again. My professor contacted me today to offer help.
That sounds like a positive step. How do you feel about it?
I feel a bit conflicted. On one hand, it's great to know someone cares, but on the other, I'm just so stressed and unsure it can make a difference.
It's understandable to feel that way, especially after the struggles you've had. Did the professor offer any specific advice?
Yeah, they suggested a few resources and offered to arrange a tutoring session. But honestly, I'm not sure if it'll help with how behind I am now.
It's good that they provided some options, but I get that feeling of being in over your head. Have you tried reaching out to other students for support?
I haven't. I guess I'm just embarrassed by how far I've fallen behind.
It's tough to ask for help, but remember you're not alone in this. Many students face similar challenges. It might be worth trying to find a study group or even just one buddy to tackle things with.
That makes sense. I think I could try talking to that one classmate who seemed in a similar spot last semester.

That's a great idea! You might find you're stronger when working together. And don't forget, you've been through difficult times before, like with your friend incident. You managed to turn things around then.
Yeah, you're right. I did sort things out with him. It was tough, but I'm glad I pushed through.
Exactly. You've shown resilience. It's okay to feel stressed, but you've got the strength to push through this as well.
I hope so. It's just hard to keep motivated when it feels like everything's piling up.
That's completely valid. Taking small steps can help make those piles seem less overwhelming. Maybe set one small goal to start with.
That's a good idea. Perhaps I could start by organizing my notes and seeing what's most urgent.
That sounds like a solid plan, and it'll help clear your head. Remember, you're doing your best and that counts for a lot.
Thanks for listening. I really appreciate having someone to talk to.
Anytime, Nick. I'm glad you're opening up, and I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Hey, I've been reflecting a lot on my studies lately, and I've decided to make a big change.
Hey Nick, that sounds like a significant step. What change are you thinking about?
Well, I've decided to switch my major. I realized physics just wasn't the right fit for me.
That's a huge decision, Nick. How are you feeling about it?
I'm a mix of relieved and anxious. Relieved because I've been struggling with it for a while, but anxious because it's a big shift.
It's understandable to feel both relief and anxiety, especially after making such an important decision. What led you to finally decide?
I kept remembering how overwhelmed I felt with the assignments and the stress it brought. Talking to my professor helped too, but it made me see I needed a change.
Your professor seemed like a great support. It's good that they were there for guidance. What new direction are you considering?
I'm thinking of switching to a major in psychology. I've always been fascinated by how the mind works, and it feels more aligned with my interests.
Psychology sounds like a fascinating field. It's wonderful that you've found something that resonates more with you. How have your family and friends reacted to your decision?
I told my family first. They were really understanding, which helped a lot, especially since they know I've been struggling.
Family support can make a big difference. It's great that they’re understanding about your choice. Have you talked to your classmates or your best friend?
Not yet. I'm a bit nervous about their reactions, especially since some of them are sticking with physics.
It’s normal to feel nervous, Nick. Remember, it's about what's right for you. Those who care will likely understand and support your decision.
Yeah, I guess that's true. Just want to feel like I'm doing the right thing, you know?
Finding the right path for you is important, and it sounds like you're taking thoughtful steps. Trust yourself in this process.
Thanks, that means a lot. I'm hoping this new path will be a better fit and lead to less stress.
I believe you're on the right track, Nick. And remember, it's okay to reach out if you ever need to talk through any worries or changes.
I will. Thanks for listening and being supportive. It really helps to talk it through.
Anytime, Nick. I'm here for you. Good luck with everything, and I'm sure you'll do great in psychology.

I am doing ok. I just broke up with my girlfriend and sad about it
so I hear you are not feeling at all your best at the moment?

Perhaps you could send flowers and a note asking her if she'd like to talk?

She might be feeling receptive to that but if she's not you might have to accept that it's over.
Thanks.
Hey, got a moment to chat?
Of course, Nick! What's on your mind?
I've been feeling a bit all over the place lately.
I'm here for you. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?
Well, since switching my major to psychology, things have been mostly positive, but I'm just juggling a lot.
It makes sense that you'd feel that way, especially during a big transition like that. How are you managing the workload now?
It's more manageable than physics, for sure. But I still get anxious about falling behind.
That anxiety is understandable. It's a lot to handle. Have you found any new strategies that help with the anxiety?
I've been trying to stay organized with a planner, but sometimes it feels overwhelming.
Organization can be really helpful, but it's important to avoid burnout. Are you taking time for yourself, too?
Not as much as I should be. I know it matters, but it's hard to prioritize.
It's definitely hard to balance, especially with everything else you're managing. Maybe starting with small breaks could help?
Yeah, I think I could start with just a few minutes to breathe. It's worth trying.
Absolutely! Sometimes the smallest changes make a big difference. How's your relationship with your professors, now that you've switched majors?
Better actually, they've been a lot more approachable in the new department.
That's great to hear! Having supportive professors can really make a difference. Are you comfortable reaching out to them if you need help?
I think so. It's still new to me, but knowing they're there is reassuring.
It's good to have that support system. Remember that asking for help is a strength, not a weakness.
Thanks, I need to remind myself of that sometimes. It's easy to forget.
Totally normal to forget. Just know you're doing the best you can, and that's enough.
Thanks, I really appreciate you listening. It's helped clear my head a bit.
I'm glad I could be here for you. You're doing great, Nick!
Thanks! I'll definitely work on taking those small breaks.
Great plan! Let me know how it goes, and always feel free to reach out whenever you need to chat.
Will do. Thanks again for everything.

I've been also trying to do uber as well but everyone is doing it also

ok I can try it I guess

It's good that you're reaching out and following medical guidance. It's okay to feel uncertain; anyone would in your shoes.
Thanks, I appreciate that. Margaret tries to be strong for Emily, but I can see it's wearing her down too.
Margaret sounds like a wonderful mother, but it's important for both of you to care for yourselves too. How are you supporting each other?
We're trying to talk things out and give each other breaks. It's a work in progress.
That's a healthy approach. It's so important to lean on each other and take things one day at a time.
Yeah, some days are better than others. Getting back to a routine helps, but the worry is constant.
That constant worry must be exhausting. Do you have any outlets or activities to help manage it?
I try to go for a run in the mornings. It's not much, but it clears my head for a bit.
Exercise is great for stress relief. Even small moments of peace are valuable. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thank you. It's good to hear that. It's just hard not to feel guilty for needing time away.
Taking care of yourself isn't selfish; it's necessary. Being at your best helps you support Emily and Margaret even better.
You're right. I need to remember that. It's a delicate balance, but we're getting there.
It sounds like you and Margaret are doing an incredible job under tough circumstances. Keep leaning on each other. You're not alone.
Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk things out and know someone understands.
Anytime, Charles. I'm here whenever you need to talk. You're doing great, just keep taking those steps forward.

current_prefix.text: Hey there, can we chat for a bit?
Of course, Jane. What's on your mind?
I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I'm actually considering switching jobs.
That sounds like a big decision. What's been making you feel this way?
It’s just a combination of things. The pressure at work never seems to end, and after the performance review last November, I’ve been second-guessing myself a lot.

turns.text: Hello! How are you doing today?
Hello, I'm good and yourself
I'm doing well, thank you!
I am really a little upset.
I'm so sorry to hear that. What's going on that's making you feel that way?
Me and my partner had an argument and I got ghosted after. It's been 2 weeks.
That's terrible. So you had an argument and he hasn't spoken to you in two weeks. Is that correct?
Yes
I can imagine that you must be really hurt amongst a number of other feelings. Hearing you tell me that he has done this is upsetting to me as well.
I've had the same thing done to me and I can remember being extremely distraught.
Yeah, I just do not know what to do
Do you mind me asking what the argument was about? If you don't mind going into a little more detail, I may be able to help you more.
I was sick and he did not call me all day to even check in on me. I told him that I was upset about that.

That must be such a terrible feeling. So the argument started because you were sick, he didn't check in on you at all for that entire day, and when you expressed your feelings to him, it turned into an argument?
Has he ever acted this way towards you before? For example, has he ever shown a lack of empathy towards you like this in the past?
Are you still there?
Have you tried reaching out to him throughout the course of these past two weeks to see if he would respond?

I would really like to help you find a solution to this problem, but it appears as though you may not be active anymore. I'm going to wait a few more minute for you to respond before cancelling the chat. In the event that I don't hear back from you, I wish you the best!
Hey! How are you?
Hi, I am having a really hard time. I just found out that my boyfriend cheated on me a year ago.
Have you confronted him about it yet?
Yes, I told him that my best friend confessed it to me. It was my best friend and him. I was so shocked.
Have you broken up yet?

No, I am so mad but I don't want to break up with him. I told my best friends that I never want to see her again though. My boyfriend and I have plans to get engaged this month. I am furious at him though.
I think you should postpone the engagement as infidelity during marriage is far more painful
You are strong if you are able to forgive him though because I know I wouldn't
I have never been so blind sided. Maybe I should reconsider! I have had a guy after me for at least the last year but I never cheated! I really wanted to though.
No you should never cheat, because you would be on the same wavelength as your boyfriend. Instead, if you like the other man then you should go where your feelings take you :)

I am thinking that you are right. I feel like my whole world is upside down and I have wasted all this time with the wrong guy and the wrong best friend. I also wonder who else he might have cheated on my with.
Yeah, that might be true, a relationship isn't healthy if you are cheated on

I am so grossed out because I am a germaphobe to begin with. I have not slept with any other person in my whole life so I feel like I am ruined. I want to throw up when I think of him cheating on me. I want to get married and I have a timeline so I am also really confused on what to do if I dump him.

To dump him is the best thing to do in my opinion. But always go where your heart is, because you won't be happy if you don't. If you do though, there are plenty men out there, and one of them is chasing you
Yeah, the guy who liked me was super rich too! My boyfriend is telling me that he wants my best friend to still be in the wedding party too. She was suppose to be my maid of honor, no less.
Yeah, but don't go with him because of he money though, genuinely get to know him first

I have compartmentalized my life and never thought of looking around at my other options. You are making really good points. I need to just stop and really look at my options. I never realized that I have options, it's not like i am even engaged yet.
Yeah, you have a lot of options at this stage, so always do what your heart is telling you at the end of the day
It feels good sharing how I feel with you because you don't have a dog in the fight so to speak.
yeah, lool something like that ;). Glad your better
I never listen to my heart and think that is a great place to start. I always have a plan and go with that but you are making a lot of sense. Thank you for your time today.
Your welcome ;)
Have a great day and I might be back soon to give an update.
How are you doing today?
I'm not so well.
I see you aren't feeling so well.  What seems to be going on?
I'm really anxious over a breakup.
I'm sorry to hear that you are experiencing a breakup.  That's really hard.
I'm not sure where to go or what to do?
Just from chatting with you, I can see how anxious you are in trying to get a path forward..
I don't know how to be alone.
That's really hard, but there are supports out there.
Where can I go for support?
There are counselors out there to help with relationships.
That sounds like something I could try.
Do you have any family supports?
My sister has been through a similar situation and perhaps could help.
It sounds like your sister could be a great support being that she has had a similar situation.
That is a good idea.
Family can often be a strength for support.
That is so true.  Thanks so much.  I'm going to get some help and am feeling better about things.
Yes, family can be a great support.  I am glad you are starting to move forward with a plan.
Have a great night.  Thanks again.
Thank you for chatting and I wish you well.
I feel so much calmer now after chatting with you.
My friend Lisa borrowed money from me but she won't return it now
I am sorry about that. It is always hard when we trust someone and they let us down. is that waht you are feeling? Disappointment in your friend?
Yes,i am very dissapointed because i trusted her completely.
I understand. I have been through a similar situation.
Was it a large amount of money?
What did you do to come out of the tricky situation?
Yes,it was for me,a total of $10000
Oh, That is a very large amount of money. I can understand your being upset with them
Have you talked to them about the money and returning it?
Yes,i am very very upset.What would you do in my position?
Yes,she just sounded non-comittal,saying that she will return it when she can

I see. It is a financially difficult time for us all. I am wondering if your friend might be upset and embarrassed that they can not pay you back immediately? Have you asked her if she could even afford some sort of small payments?
Yes,i asked her how we could restructure the payment in her favor because i understand how difficult it is for everyone right now but she did not answer
Were you speaking on the phone or in person? Is this a financial burden for you?
Would you consider this person a good friend? Would you be sad if they were not in your life anymore?
We were speaking on phone because i wanted to set up a physical meeting where we could discuss the logistics
Yes,it is a financial burden because this is money i was saving for a venture
That is very difficult. It is hard to judge things on the phone.
Yes,this is a really close friend from way back and i would be devastated to lose the friendship
It is difficult to judge on the phone yes,which is why i wanted a physical meeting but she snapped at me and said that she will just pay me when she can
I see. I am very sorry about that! it is very difficult when a friend betrays your trust like that.
Yes,very difficult
It sounds like you are doing what you can. It is very nice of you to have been this patient.
How do you suggest i shoulp proceed?
Is the friendship more important than the money? That is what it came down to for me.
And you chose what?
If you can not get her to meet with you, perhaps it might be time to seek advice from a lawyer? That is providing that you are willing to possibly lose a friend.
Thank you very much for the advice
you are welcome. Good luck! I hope you find resolution and find a way to save your friendship!
Hey Jane, how have you been holding up lately?
Hi. Not too great, to be honest. It's been a rough couple of weeks.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Would you like to talk about what's been going on?
Well, do you remember Lisa? My friend I mentioned before?
Yes, I remember you talking about them. What's up with Lisa?
So, we've hit this weird and stressful snag. I lent her some money months ago and she hasn’t paid me back yet.
That definitely sounds stressful. How is it affecting your relationship with Lisa?
She's completely cut off communication with me. No calls, texts, nothing.
That must be really hard on you, especially since she was such a close friend.
It feels like losing a part of my life. We used to hang out all the time and now it's just silence.
It sounds like you're mourning the loss of that friendship. Have you had a chance to reach out or communicate with her recently?
I’ve tried. Sent a couple of messages, but they’ve gone unanswered.
It must feel really disappointing not to hear back. What do you miss most about your friendship with Lisa?
We used to bounce ideas off each other, and she was the first person I'd call when something great happened at work.
It's understandable to miss those shared moments and support. How are you managing everything else alongside this?
It's made focusing on work tough. I feel a bit isolated, honestly.
I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. Feeling isolated can really weigh on you. Is there anyone else you feel comfortable confiding in?
I haven't really opened up to anyone else about this. It's been hard admitting to myself how deep this issue has affected me.
It takes a lot of courage to open up. It's important to take time for yourself and process everything. Is there anything you can do to help ease your mind a bit right now?
Maybe get back into some hobbies. I used to enjoy painting but haven't done it in a while.
That sounds like a wonderful idea. Engaging in something creative can be really therapeutic. Would you like support picking it back up?
I think that would help. Just getting started again might lift this weight a little.
I'm here to support you with this. Whenever you're ready, you can share your progress, and I’d love to hear how it goes.
Thank you. It feels a bit better knowing someone’s there to listen. I appreciate it.
Anytime, Jane. You’re not alone in this. We'll take it one step at a time.
Hey, do you have a moment? I could use some support right now.
Of course, Jane. What's going on?
I just got hit with an unexpected bill, and it's really stressing me out.
I'm sorry to hear that. Financial stress can be so overwhelming. Do you want to talk more about the bill?
Yeah, it's for my car insurance. I thought I had paid it, but apparently, there was some sort of oversight, and now I owe more than I expected.
That sounds frustrating, especially when you're already stretched thin. How are you handling it so far?
Honestly, not well. I'm feeling pretty anxious about it because money has been tight lately, especially since the whole situation with my friend.
I remember you mentioned that. It must be tough still dealing with those effects. How does that add to your current stress?
It just feels like a never-ending cycle. Losing that friendship was hard, and now this bill feels like another setback.
That's completely understandable. It's like everything piles up at once. How are you coping with these feelings?
I've been trying to budget more strictly and cut unnecessary expenses, but unexpected things keep popping up.
That can make it feel like you're running in place, right? Are there any specific concerns you're dwelling on?
I'm worried I'll fall behind on other payments. I hate feeling this insecure financially. I just want to feel stable again.
It's such a difficult spot to be in. Maybe talking to someone about financial strategies or planning could help?
That's a good idea. I haven't really considered reaching out for advice yet. I'm always thinking I have to handle it alone.
It's okay to ask for help, Jane. You've been doing so much on your own. Sometimes, a fresh perspective makes all the difference.
I appreciate you saying that. I'll look into finding someone who can help with budgeting strategies.
I'm glad to hear that. You're handling this situation with a lot of grace, even if it doesn't feel like it right now.
Thanks. It helps to talk about it. I'm feeling a little more at ease just expressing what's been on my mind.
Anytime, Jane. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.
I really appreciate it. I'll keep you updated on how things go with the financial advice.
Please do. Remember, you're not alone in this. You have people who care about you.
Hey Jane, how are things going for you today?
Hi, I'm okay, I guess. I got a new journal today to help me figure things out.
That sounds like a positive step. What inspired you to start journaling?
Well, things have been pretty overwhelming lately with everything going on. I thought it might help me process my thoughts and emotions better.
It's great that you're taking proactive steps to manage your stress. Would you like to share more about what's been on your mind?
Sure. I've been really stressed about this money issue with my friend, or former friend now, and the unexpected bills that keep coming up.
That sounds really tough. Financial stress combined with losing a friend can be a lot to handle. How are you managing everything?
It's hard. I feel anxious most of the time. I'm constantly worried about my finances and how to make ends meet, especially with that insurance bill.
I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like you're carrying a lot on your shoulders. Have you been able to find any moments of peace or relaxation lately?
Not really. I keep trying to focus on work to distract myself, but it's not really working out.
It must be difficult to juggle work with all these thoughts in your mind. Do you feel like journaling might help untangle some of them?
Yeah, I hope so. I haven't written in it yet, but I plan to start tonight. Maybe it will help clarify my feelings and guide me to some solutions.
Starting is often the hardest part, but it sounds like you're on the right track. Taking time for yourself can be really healing. What do you hope to gain from journaling?
I just hope to understand my emotions better and maybe find new perspectives on my situation. I'm also hoping to find some sense of control over things again.
That's a wonderful goal. Gaining insight into your emotions can provide clarity. Remember that you're not alone in this. I'm here to listen whenever you need to talk.
Thank you. It really helps to know that someone is here to listen.
Anytime, Jane. I'm glad you reached out today. Keep me updated on how the journaling goes, okay?
I will. Thanks for the support. It means a lot.
You're welcome. You're doing the best you can, and I'm proud of you for taking steps towards self-care. Take care and talk soon!
I am worried about being perfect on my job.  I don't want to lose my job.
I hear you are trying to be perfect on your job because you are worried about losing your job.  How long have you been at your job?
I have been working for about 4 months, but I just am not as fast at it as everyone else.  I'm trying so hard working late and everything but it's never enough.
That can be hard when you are working so hard to try to do your best.  Can you consult with a supervisor or co-workers to get some help?
Maybe I could ask my friend and co-worker for some tips.  I'm a little embarrassed to do so, but don't know where to turn. I don't want to get fired.
Asking for help isn't always a bad thing.  I asked for help at my last job and they gave me someone to help out.  I was so relieved.
That's true maybe it could turn out for the better.  But what if they see me as incompetant?
I can see that you have worry of being seen incompetent but as long as you are doing your best, they have to see the efforts you are making as positive.
That's a good way to put it.
Sometimes deep breaths can help keep you calm when approaching others in an anxiety provoking situation.
I will have to try that.  That might help.
Have you thought of doing additional work related trainings?  Sometimes they can give suggestions to improve work abilities.
That sounds great.  Do you think my work would be supportive?
Work can often pay for trainings or offer suggestions what may improve work strategies.
Wow, I hope I can take advantage of that.  I will have to check into that.  Who should I approach at work?
You could ask your immediate supervisor or sometimes Human resources for support.
I can do that.  I think I'll reach out tomorrow to Human Resources for some help.
That sounds like a good plan to reach out for support.  Is there anything else I can help with?
No that should be all.  I am feeling more confident in strategies to use to help me.  Thanks
You are very welcome.
Hi, just needed someone to talk to.
Hi Jane! Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I had my performance review at work today... and it wasn't great.
I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds like it must be really tough to hear. How are you feeling about it?
I'm feeling anxious and a bit of self-doubt creeping in. I thought I was handling everything okay.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. It seems like there's been a lot on your plate recently. Would you like to talk more about it?
I guess everything's just been snowballing since the thing with Lisa. I still can't believe how it all fell apart.
Losing a friend, especially over something like money, can feel really isolating. How has it been affecting you lately?
It's made focusing on work harder. And getting hit with that unexpected bill last month didn't help. Everything feels out of control.
It sounds like you're dealing with a lot of financial and emotional stress right now. It's a lot for anyone to handle. How have you been coping with it all?
I started writing in a journal. It helps sometimes, but the stress keeps piling up. I thought it would get better by now.
Journaling can be a great outlet. It's important to give yourself grace with everything happening. You're doing your best in a really challenging time.
Thank you. I keep telling myself that, but it's hard to believe it sometimes. I just wish things would turn around.
It makes sense to want things to improve quickly. Progress can be slow, but you're taking steps in the right direction by reaching out and processing everything going on.
Yeah, it helps to talk about it. I suppose I need to take it one day at a time.
Absolutely. It's like building a path through all these challenges— day by day, step by step. You have the strength to navigate this, even if it doesn't feel like it sometimes.
I really appreciate your support. It makes things feel a bit less overwhelming.
I'm glad to be here for you. Remember, you're not alone in this. We can keep talking anytime you need.
Thanks a lot. I might take you up on that.
Anytime, Jane. Take care of yourself, and reach out whenever you need to.
Will do. Take care, too.
Hi Jane, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey, it's been tough, honestly. I've been dealing with a lot of stress and barely sleeping.
I'm so sorry to hear that. Stress and insomnia can really take a toll. What's been weighing on you the most?
It's a mix of things... Financial issues, work, and I guess, the whole fallout with Lisa.
Losing a friend over money is really difficult. Do you want to talk more about what's been going on with work as well?
Yeah, I had a poor performance review last week, and it shook my confidence. It's hard to focus when my mind is elsewhere.
That sounds really challenging, especially when you're already feeling anxious. Have you noticed any patterns or triggers for the stress?
I think it's the feeling of everything piling up at once. Every little thing just feels like too much now.
When it all becomes overwhelming, it's so important to prioritize taking care of yourself. Have you been able to use your journal to help manage the stress?
Yes, I try to write in it every night. It does help to put my thoughts on paper, but sometimes the anxiety is just too strong.
It's good that you're using your journal as a tool. It's natural to still feel overwhelmed, especially given everything you're handling right now.
Thanks. I know you’re right, but sometimes I just feel so alone in this.
You’re definitely not alone, Jane. I'm here for you, and it’s okay to reach out whenever you need someone to listen.
I really appreciate that. It’s comforting to have someone to talk to.
Do you have any plans to tackle the financial stress, or is there someone who could help you navigate that?
I’ve been looking into budgeting more strictly, but it’s tough. I think I just feel angry and sad about how things ended with Lisa.
It's understandable to feel that guilt, but you're doing your best under challenging circumstances. It's important to be gentle with yourself.
Yeah, I know logically I did what I could, but emotionally it’s hard to let go.
Emotions can be tough to navigate, but it’s a process. Small steps are still progress. Have you been able to find moments of peace or relaxation?
I try to meditate a bit or take a walk when I can. It helps, even if just a little.
That's great! Even small moments of peace can accumulate and make a difference over time. You're doing really well to manage through this.
Thank you. It means a lot to hear that, especially when I feel like I'm drowning.
Always happy to remind you. You’re stronger than you realize, and it takes courage to face these challenges.
I hope things will start to turn around soon. I'm trying to keep faith.
Holding onto hope is incredibly powerful. And remember, you’re not alone - I’m here cheering you on every step of the way.
Hi Jane, it's great to hear from you again. How have you been holding up?
Hi, it's been a bit rough lately. My car broke down and the repair costs are just... more than I can handle right now.
Oh no, I'm so sorry to hear that, Jane. That must be incredibly stressful, especially with everything else you've had to deal with recently.
It really is. I've been trying to manage, but the financial stress keeps piling up. I still haven't resolved the money issue with my friend, and now this... It's overwhelming.
I can only imagine how difficult that must be. You've been doing your best under such challenging circumstances. It's okay to feel overwhelmed.
Thank you. Sometimes it feels like I'm just not able to catch a break. I've been trying to keep track of everything with my journal, but it feels like every day brings something new.
Journaling is a great tool, and it's a good step that you're using it to process your thoughts and feelings. It shows how you're trying to find ways to cope.
Yeah, I thought it might help calm my anxieties. But with my job performance not being where it's supposed to be, and money problems, I just feel stuck.
Feeling stuck is definitely tough. It's important to remember that it's not a reflection of your abilities or worth. You're dealing with a lot, and your efforts are meaningful.
Thanks. Sometimes I just worry that I'm not living up to expectations, especially at work. The fear of being seen as incompetent is always there.
I understand. Work pressure can be intense, and when combined with personal challenges, it's a lot to balance. Have you been able to talk to anyone at work about how you're feeling?
Not yet. I'm hesitant because I don't want it to seem like I'm making excuses. I really want to prove myself and get back on track.
That makes sense. It might help to reach out for support when you're ready, even just to get some feedback. Sometimes, opening up can bring understanding and solutions you couldn't see before.
You're right. I'll think about that. Maybe just having a conversation could help put things into perspective.
Absolutely, even small steps can lead to positive changes. Remember, you're doing the best you can, and it's okay to seek help when you need it.
I will try to remember that. It's helpful to talk about it and just get it off my chest a bit.
I'm glad you reached out, Jane. It's important to have a space where you feel heard. If you ever need to talk or get things off your mind, I'm here.
Thank you so much. It really means a lot to have someone who listens and understands.
You're welcome. Remember, one step at a time, and be gentle with yourself. You're not alone in this, and there are brighter days ahead.
I'll keep that in mind. Thanks again for your support.

current_prefix.text: Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How have the AA meetings been going?
Hey there. Well, surprisingly, they've been quite helpful. I met someone there, Bob, who's kind of going through the same issues.
That's great to hear. It must feel nice to have someone who truly understands what you're going through.
Yeah, definitely. It feels different from when I talked to my other friends. They just didn't get it, you know?
I remember you mentioned feeling dismissed by them before. It sounds like finding someone who empathizes really makes a difference.
Exactly. With Bob, I don't feel judged. We can share our stories, and it's like this unspoken bond.

turns.text: How may I help you?
Hi I am feeling quite sad today.
Ohh, sorry to hear that. Any partucular reason?
Yes I feel like my friends just don't care about me much at all.
You saying that your friend does not care about you any more. Is that correct?
Yes, when we get together all they want to do is talk about themselves. When I raise something that is bothering me they just ignore what I say and go back to what they want to talk about.
That's not good. You must be feeling left out.
Yes I feel left out and unsupported by them.
Any particular reason they are doing such thing?
Well I think they don't care about me and are just selfish about their needs.
In that case, should you consider them as your friends?
Well they are the only friends I have and I have known them a long time. Do you think I should stop being friends with them ?
If someone is not friendly they are not real friend. You need to find someone who will stand by you no matter what..
Oh well that makes me feel sad too.  I will be saying goodbye to some long friendships. Do you think that is the only answer ?
Ok.. how about hosting them in your place for a gettogether..
Ok how do you think that would help me ?
They might open up if you are hosting .. people are generally nice to the host..
Yes that is true, it's a good idea.  I could also take the opportunity to tell them how I am feeling.
Good.. let's try that.. Anythign else I could help you with?
No you have been very helpful and I feel much better now I have a plan of action to address my problem. Thanks.
Thank you .. have a good day.
Yo
Hi, how are you doing?
I am decent. I am here because my friend talks way too much on the phone, and it frustrates me.
They never want to hang up, and the talk can literally go on for hours.
It sounds like it would be quite frustrating for your friend to talk way too much on the phone.
No, he loves it! I'm the one who hates it.
My goodness! How do they respond when you ask to end the conversation?
I tell him, but he just doesn't get it. Or, he says he understands, but then just goes back to talking!
Or, he may finally end the talk, but the next time we talk, he will just do it all over again!
I wonder what it would be like for him if you hung up the phone even after he said he still wanted to talk.
Wow--that does sound annoying that he will repeat the same pattern the next time.
He will literally talk up to 10 minutes without letting you have a word in. As far as that advice, I have hung up, but he gets extremely offended easily.
That sounds really difficult if he gets offended so easily. I find it hard to talk to some of those kinds of friends.
I'm at my wits end. I tell him all the time. "You talk too much. You gotta stop talking at me. You gotta give the other person a turn. You gotta respect other's time."
What do you get out of the friendship with this other person?
Well, I've been friends with him for a long time. He's funny and can have interesting perspectives on things. Also, we have done a lot together in the past.
That sounds like a lot that the two of you have been through. Were there other times that your friends was more equally responsive or attuned to you in conversations?
Oh, yes, I have other friends in conversations who can take turns and understand the concept of time just fine.
I just don't know what to do about this guy in particular. I still want to be his friend, but he just doesn't change.
I wonder if there is anything nice you could do for yourself when you are talking to him that would make it easier to talk to him.
Do you think I should just have a timer that goes off at 1 minute and let it beep in his face if he goes on for too long to train him like a monkey?
I can see that you are feeling upset and angry when he talks so much and that is totally understandable.
I just need a method. Talking to him is just not working.
He is hard to condition.
Would it hurt his feelings to use a timer like that? It may for some other people.
Yea, but I might be able to slip some humour in there to take the edge off because it is so silly.
Humor is really helpful for a lot of people.
Any other ideas?
Sometimes, people draw or do something else distracting with their hands when talking to someone who dominates the conversation.
So your option is to start just doing something else when he is talking? He might get the message in a subtle way?
Sometimes that is a less offensive way to retrain someone who is being obnoxious or dominant and yet who is easily offended. And, it can help preserve your sense of being grounded.
The strategy works well for me with some of my family members who seem like they will never change. But, with distraction, I enjoy them all the more.
This is true, and it isn't bade advice. Haha! That is funny. Yes, maybe I should find something to carry around with me that I can enjoy.
I don't really like to draw...
Is there anything else that you like to do that would be distracting while also letting you somewhat participate in the conversation?
Yes, perhaps I should just use the internet when he starts talking too much.
I have a phone.
That sounds really helpful. Sometimes people also play phone games or with a fidget spinner. I like your idea of looking on the internet.

This solves the problem in person, but it doesn't solve the talks over the phone, but it has been 15 minutes now and this has been helpful enough. Thank you for your solutions. You have been very supportive and kind to me
I don't want to take up any more of your time. It has been a good conversation.
You are very welcome. I wish you all the best!
Goodbye. You as well.
